scenes.label: JATINGA, ASSAM
lines: In a small hill village in Assam, birds fall out of the night sky.
It happens between September and November, on dark, foggy evenings, roughly between six and half past nine.

scenes.label: 49 SPECIES
lines: Forty-nine kinds of birds are involved, mostly young ones. Herons, kingfishers, pigeons.
They fly straight toward the village lights, and come down dazed.
For years, it was called the valley where birds commit suicide.

scenes.label: THE TWIST
lines: But scientists say the birds are not choosing to die.
Strong winds and fog disorient them, and they fly toward lights, looking for shelter.
Many of the deaths came when people struck the dazed birds with bamboo poles. The real mystery was never the birds.
Follow for one mystery every day.

youtube.description:
Every autumn, in Jatinga (Dima Hasao district, Assam), birds come down out of the sky toward the village lights on dark, foggy nights, usually between about 6 p.m. and 9:30 p.m., from September to November. It was once called 'bird suicide'. Researchers, including ornithologist Anwaruddin Choudhury, concluded the birds are disoriented by high winds and fog and fly toward lights seeking refuge, and that most deaths were caused by people killing the dazed birds. Conservation work has since tried to stop the killing. All visuals are original illustrations.
